title: Principles You Can See
subtitle: Four engineering principles, shown on one real project
notes: Spoken text uses Gemini TTS tags <short pause> and <long pause>; subtitles strip them. Numbers are spelled as spoken; visuals show digits. The principles are named 'our principles'; no organisation is named.

principles.name: Everything as code
principles.tagline: If it matters, it lives in the repo.

principles.name: Own the decision
principles.tagline: Decide in the open. Own the outcome.

principles.name: Stay relevant
principles.tagline: The market moves. So do we.

beats.text: Every team has principles. They hang on a wall, or sit in a slide deck. <short pause> And then Monday starts.
beats.visual: A poster on a wall with four short lines. A calendar card 'Monday' pops in; a busy desk slides in front of the poster.

beats.text: So what do principles look like in real work? Not on a slide, but in a repository?
beats.visual: The poster folds up and drops into a repository folder icon.

beats.text: Meet Tip again. Tip is a small iceberg, and today Tip shows you four of our principles, using one real project.
beats.visual: Camera pans down to the sea. Tip bobs up and waves; four layers under the water glow faintly, still unlabelled.

beats.text: The Iceberg Data Platform: an open data platform that I build together with an AI agent.
beats.visual: A project card: 'Iceberg Data Platform', with small building-block chips (catalog, storage, sign-in, engine, workspace) and the agent next to a person.

beats.text: Four principles. <short pause> Four places to look.
beats.visual: Title 'Principles You Can See'. The four layers get their labels: AI Native, Everything as code, Own the decision, Stay relevant.

beats.text: Principle one: AI native. <short pause> AI operates. You architect.
beats.visual: Zoom into the first layer. Big tile 'AI Native' with the tagline 'AI operates. You architect.'

beats.text: You put AI to work on what it's good at: code, tests, analysis and first drafts. You stay accountable for the framing, the trade-offs, and everything that goes live.
beats.visual: Two columns. Left, the agent with four cards: Code, Tests, Analysis, First drafts. Right, a person with three cards: Framing, Trade-offs, What goes live.

beats.text: In the platform, an AI agent writes most of the code, the tests and the first drafts of the designs.
beats.visual: The agent at work: code lines stream, test ticks pop, a design draft fills in.

beats.text: But the real questions come back to a person. Kubernetes now, or only a design? A two-hour token, or a setting? Each answer is a human call.
beats.visual: Two question cards with two options each. A person's hand picks 'Only a design' and 'A setting'.

beats.text: And nothing goes live on the agent's word. A release only ships when a person tags it, and only after the full test run passes.
beats.visual: A person places a version tag 'v0.8.0'. A row of test steps lights up green; then the release box opens.

beats.text: Principle two: everything as code. <short pause> If it matters, it lives in the repo.
beats.visual: Tile 'Everything as code' with the tagline. A repository box opens.

beats.text: Docs, deployments and architecture are versioned, reviewed and diffable. Nothing important lives in a wiki page, a console click, or somebody's head.
beats.visual: Three things outside the repo, a wiki page, a mouse click and a head with a thought, turn grey and get a cross. Docs, a deployment file and a diagram fly into the repo.

beats.text: In the platform, the docs sit next to the code. The installer, the deployment and the release pipeline are files in the same repository.
beats.visual: A repository tree builds up: README.md, docs/, compose.yaml, install.sh, .github/workflows/.

beats.text: Even the contracts between the parts are files. If the code and its contract drift apart, a test fails.
beats.visual: An openapi.yaml card paired with a code card; they drift apart and a red test cross pops.

beats.text: The agent's instructions live there too, in an agents file and a set of skills. <short pause> And so does this video: its script, its sources and its music are code.
beats.visual: AGENTS.md and SKILL.md cards slide into the repo, then a film strip with a code symbol.

beats.text: Principle three: own the decision. <short pause> Decide in the open. Own the outcome.
beats.visual: Tile 'Own the decision' with the tagline.

beats.text: Write down why, not just what. Build it, and run it. And design for composability and portability, so today's choice never becomes tomorrow's cage.
beats.visual: Three icons in spoken order: a 'WHY' document, a gauge for running it, connected blocks. A cage around a block opens and fades.

beats.text: Big choices in the platform get a decision record: what we chose, what we didn't choose, and why.
beats.visual: A decision record with three sections lighting up: Chosen, Not chosen, Why.

beats.text: For example, pipeline runs get no internet, on purpose. The record says why, so nobody has to guess later.
beats.visual: A run box with a padlock 'no internet'; a WHY stamp lands on the record.

beats.text: We run what we build: an infrastructure page shows the health of every container, extensions included.
beats.visual: A dashboard with rows of services, each with a green health dot and small resource bars.

beats.text: And the parts talk through open standards: Iceberg tables, S3 storage, OpenID Connect for sign-in, and MCP for agents. So one part can be replaced without touching the others.
beats.visual: Four plugs labelled Iceberg, S3, OpenID Connect, MCP connect blocks. One block slides out and a new one slides in.

beats.text: Principle four: stay relevant. <short pause> The market moves. So do we.
beats.visual: Tile 'Stay relevant' with the tagline; a moving stream of tool logos-as-shapes in the background (no real logos).

beats.text: Own the capability roadmap, not the tool roadmap. Every tool we run has a successor, and an exit date we set ourselves.
beats.visual: A road with milestones labelled by capability; tool chips ride on it. A small calendar with a date we pin ourselves.

beats.text: The platform is a map of capabilities: a catalog, storage, sign-in, an engine, and a place to work. Each one is filled by a tool, and each tool can be swapped.
beats.visual: Five capability slots with tool chips: Catalog · Polaris, Storage · RustFS, Sign-in · Keycloak, Engine · DuckDB, Workspace · marimo. One chip slides out and back in.

beats.text: Bots check the dependencies every week. And before this release, an agent swept the repository for anything that had gone stale. Thirteen releases in just over three weeks.
beats.visual: A weekly calendar with a small bot ticking off updates; a broom sweeps dust out of a repo box; counter ticks to 13 releases.

beats.text: Design records name the successor before it's needed: pipeline runs use Docker today, and a Kubernetes design is ready for later.
beats.visual: Two cards on a road: 'Today · Docker' and 'Next · Kubernetes (design ready)'.

beats.text: And the contract between the parts has a written policy: from version one, an old version keeps running next to the new one for at least a release. We set the exit date.
beats.visual: Two contract cards 'v1' and 'v2' side by side; a calendar pin marks the exit date, placed by a person.

beats.text: Four principles. <short pause> AI operates, you architect. If it matters, it's in the repo. Decide in the open. And keep moving.
beats.visual: The four tiles pop in one by one, in spoken order.

beats.text: None of them needs a poster to be true. Each one shows up in a file, a test, or a decision you can read.
beats.visual: The poster from scene 1 dissolves into three glowing items: a file, a test tick, a decision record.

beats.text: So next Monday, open your repository and ask: where can someone see our principles at work?
beats.visual: Back at the desk on Monday; the laptop shows a repository; a question bubble.

beats.text: If the answer is everywhere, they're under the water, holding everything up.
beats.visual: Back to the sea: Tip on top of four lit layers labelled with the principles. Title returns; transition to the end card.

endCard.title: Principles You Can See
